name: meteor-shower
about: Our own painting: a moonless night over a mountain lake at the height of a meteor shower. The streaks pour out of the radiant, a knot of bright stars high on the left, every one on a ray from it: a long fireball crossing to the right with its twisted train, a fan of shorter streaks below it and faint ones between, each brightening to a white-green head with a violet tail. Behind them the sky is still: a deep indigo night thick with stars, the Milky Way climbing from the lower left with its dark rift, a faint green airglow low over the range; the range's snow caps and crests catch the starlight and a still lake holds them, a dark mirror (painters/meteors.py; shipped as a JPEG). The first jewel is the indigo night, the second the airglow's teal over the range and, faint, in the lake under it (MR 6 round 1: teal rather than green, and the lake's at chroma 0.04, since the green on the water read as a striped field, game designer m1, and a protanope saw the green airglow as the orange's grey, UX m2).
